text:
FATF Gives Singapore Top AML Rating But Flags Penalty Weaknesses
The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) has granted Singapore its highest rating for its anti-money laundering framework, according to a Mutual Evaluation report released on Wednesday, May 6.
The periodic review, which assessed Singapore’s measures to combat financial crime, concluded that the city-state maintains a robust system for preventing the misuse of its financial infrastructure. The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) noted that the findings underscore the country’s effectiveness in combatting financial crime.
A central component of the FATF’s assessment was the high-profile S$3 billion money laundering case that emerged in 2023. The watchdog described this case as “the clearest manifestation of Singapore’s ongoing and active implementation of incremental and unique measures to take on those attempting to misuse Singapore’s financial system.”
According to the report, the 2023 crackdown—which involved foreign nationals who moved billions derived from overseas remote gambling offences—served as a dual indicator. While it highlighted Singapore’s continued attractiveness to international criminals, the FATF stated it as well demonstrated the quality of the city-state’s law enforcement and the political commitment of the government to tackling financial crime.
Despite the top rating, the FATF identified specific shortcomings that require attention. The global watchdog flagged weaknesses in the severity of penalties imposed for money laundering, suggesting that Singapore needs harsher penalties to act as a more effective deterrent.
The evaluation also pointed to gaps in cross-border cooperation. The report indicated that while internal frameworks are strong, the effectiveness of Singapore’s response to financial crime is hindered by these deficiencies in international collaboration and the current scale of its penal sanctions.
The review covered the period from 2020 through July 2025, analyzing the evolution of the country’s anti-money laundering, countering terrorist financing, and proliferation financing measures.
The FATF’s findings leave Singapore with the task of addressing the identified gaps in its penal system and enhancing its cooperative mechanisms with foreign jurisdictions.
